title: Bridging the Divide: End-to-End Sequence-Graph Learning
abstract: arXiv:2510.25126v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Many real-world prediction tasks, particularly those involving entities such as customers or patients, involve both {sequential} and {relational} data. Each entity maintains its own sequence of events while simultaneously engaging in relationships with others. Existing methods in sequence and graph modeling often overlook one modality in favor of the other. We argue that these two facets should instead be integrated and learned jointly. We introduce BRIDGE, a unified end-to-end architecture that couples a sequence model with a graph module under a single objective, allowing gradients to flow across both components to learn task-aligned representations. To enable fine-grained interaction, we propose TOKENXATTN, a token-level cross-attention layer that facilitates message passing between specific events in neighboring sequences. translated_title: 跨越鸿沟：端到端序列-图学习
translated_abstract: 许多现实世界的预测任务，尤其是涉及客户或患者等实体的任务，同时包含序列数据和关系数据。每个实体既维护着自己的事件序列，又同时与其他实体保持着关联关系。现有的序列建模与图建模方法往往偏重其中一种模态而忽视另一种。我们认为这两种维度应当被整合起来并进行联合学习。我们提出了BRIDGE，这是一种统一的端到端架构，它在单一目标下将序列模型与图模块耦合在一起，使梯度能够在两个组件之间流动，从而学习与任务对齐的表示。为了实现细粒度的交互，我们提出了TOKENXATTN，这是一种词元级的交叉注意力层，能够在相邻序列中的特定事件之间进行消息传递。在关系预测和欺诈检测两种任务场景中，BRIDGE始终优于现有基线方法。
tldr: 提出了BRIDGE统一端到端架构，在单一目标下联合学习序列模型与图模块，并通过词元级交叉注意力实现相邻序列事件间的细粒度消息传递，在关系预测和欺诈检测任务上表现优异。
en_tdlr: BRIDGE is a unified end-to-end architecture that jointly learns sequence and graph representations under a single objective, leveraging token-level cross-attention for fine-grained message passing between events, consistently outperforming baselines on relationship prediction and fraud detection tasks.
